To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

N9-substitution of the purine ring by various functionalized alkyl chains, which are able to interact with the purine moiety via hydrogen bond, does not affect cytokinin activity of N(6)-(3-methylbutenyl)amino-purine derivatives, and that the cytokinin activity of these derivatives is not correlated with their ability to activate cytokinin receptor CRE1/Ahk4 from Arabidoposis.

N(6)-substituted derivatives of iP are active in Amaranthus and tobacco callus bio-assays and that N(9) substituents of the purine ring do not affect cytokinin activity of N(6)-(3-methylbutenyl)amino) derivatives.
the majority of prepared derivatives are active in Amaranthus and tobacco callus bioassy but inactive in detached wheat senescence bioassay.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the synthesis and biological activity of a series of N(9)-substituted iP derivatives in selected cytokinin in vitro bioassay and cytokinin receptor activation.
the preparation of N9-substituted iP derivatives and their biological evaluation in three different in vitro cytokinin assays.
a new group of cytokinin derivatives with various substituents at the N9-atom of the purine moiety.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the substitution of the purine moiety at the N9 position with the tetrahydropyranyl group (compound 1) is the only one that can trigger cytokinin activity in the majority of the bioassays, and also in the cytokinin receptor CRE1/AKH4.
the N9-alkylated derivatives are active in both Amarnathus as well as in the tobacco callus bioassy, and that the N9-substitution is not a prerequisite for the cytokinin activity of iP derivatives.

cytokinin activity of N(6) substituted iP derivatives is not only determined by the presence of N6-substituent, but also by the nature of N(6)-(3-methylbuten-1-yl)-substituent and the type of N9 substituent, which may have an effect on the cytokinin activity of these derivatives.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
N(9)-tetrahydropyranyl substituted iP derivatives were active in all bioassays tested and in the majority of cases they were more potent than the unsubstituted iP (1) itself.

N9-substituted iP derivatives are active cytokinins in selected cytokinin-sensitive bioassays and that their activity is not directly linked to the ability of the derivatives to trigger the cytokinine response in the cytokinin receptor CRE1/AKH4.
the substitution of N9 atom by a tetrahydropyranyl moiety is the best way to increase cytokinin activity of iP derivatives in both Amaranth and tobacco bioassays.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of a functional group on the C3 atom of tetrahydropyranyl moiety is not necessary for the activity of the compound.
N9-substituted iP derivatives were not able to induce cytokinin response in the cytokinin-sensitive CRE1/AHK3 and ZmHK receptors, but were able to activate cytokinin response in maize ZmHk3a.
the cytokinin response of the prepared derivatives in the bioassays was not related to the recognition by cytokinin receptors CRE1/AHK, ZmHK1, and ZmHKa.
